newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street set to open mixed, eyes futures, FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street set to open mixed, eyes futures, FOMC.

text.p: Wall Street was expected to open mixed, with trading likely to be choppy as players try to assess which way the market is heading, traders said.
"A lot of the market will depend on how the futures act," said Arnie Owen, managing director of capitial markets at Cruttenden Roth.
S&P 500 September futures were fluctuating between the negative and positive columns ahead of the Dow's opening.
Although nobody expected the Fed to alter interest rates at today's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, confirmation of the outcome at about 1415 EDT/1815 GMT was keenly awaited.
The long bond remained weaker, off 6/32 to yield 6.54 percent, but the dollar enjoyed a steadier tone.
U.S. housing starts in July came in at 1.447 million units on an annual basis, unchanged from June. Analysts had expected starts at a 1.46 million rate in July.

Doug Myers, vice president of equity trading at Interstate/Johnson Lane, said early trading was likely to be choppy as players sought direction after Monday's 108-point rebound which had been "too far and too quick."
